page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-224 is a general-purpose server powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 224 vCPUs mapped to 112 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 896 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4 GB of RAM per core. This configuration does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 10% of tested instances. Memory performance is also strong, with cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 12,510.38 GB/sec and Passmark memory scores placing in the top 10%. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with Geekbench single-core and text processing benchmarks falling into the average tier.

The server exhibits a clear performance tradeoff when handling large-scale machine learning tasks. While prompt processing for small LLM models is strong at 3,433.2 tokens/sec, text generation for large 70B models is weak, dropping to 2.56 tokens/sec due to the lack of hardware GPU acceleration. Consequently, this instance is best suited for highly parallelized, non-GPU workloads such as large-scale Redis deployments, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-224 is an x86_64 general-purpose server configured with 224 vCPUs across 112 physical AMD EPYC 7B13 cores and 896 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it relies entirely on network-attached storage. The instance delivers top-tier multi-core CPU and memory performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Passmark benchmarks ranking in the top 10%. It also excels in high-throughput operations, achieving 187.57 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core metrics and large LLM text generation speeds are average to weak, reflecting a clear tradeoff for single-threaded or AI-heavy workloads. This server is highly effective for massive parallel processing, database operations, software compilation, and high-volume web serving where high core density and memory bandwidth are required.
